title: Sectr sidecar serve mode (HTTP)
description:
The HTTP surface of `sectr-worker --serve`, the sidecar run as a server on a platform that starts a container per request (AWS Lambda through the Lambda Web Adapter, Google Cloud Run and similar). The server sends these requests to the customer's endpoint; the sidecar answers them.

Routes: `GET /` answers `identity`. `POST /wake` takes a `wakeRequest` and runs ONE invocation: it dials the image's own SECTR_INGEST_URL with the token over the Contract-4 WebSocket (sidecar.schema.json), receives the assignment and runs the turn. The request is held open until the turn ends, then answered with a `wakeResponse`. `POST /manifest` takes a `manifestRequest`, dials ingest with the token first, and only if the upgrade is accepted imports the app as managed builds do; it answers a `manifestResponse`.

The ingest URL is never taken from a request: endpoint URLs are public, so a sidecar that dialed a URL the request named could be pointed at another server. One turn at a time per instance: a request while another runs is answered 409 `busy` at once, never queued. Bodies over 4 KiB are answered 413 `too_large`; a malformed body 400 `bad_request`. The sidecar itself never answers 429 or 503: a caller may treat those as the platform saying the request never reached a container.

The wake response is never journaled; the journal says how the turn ended. Forward compatibility: additionalProperties is deliberately NOT false, and receivers ignore unknown fields.

ingestToken.description: A token minted by the Sectr server (`sit_…`). It authenticates the sidecar's dial to ingest; the request itself needs no other auth, because the dial destination is fixed by the image.

identity.description: `GET /` (200). At `/` because platform readiness checks use `/`. The version is the sidecar's (the public base image's).

wakeRequest.description: `POST /wake`: the turn's ingest token, minted at dispatch.

wakeResponse.description: `POST /wake` (200), sent when the invocation is over. `turn_ended`: a turn boundary (sentinel, approval suspension or failure; the journal holds which). `token_rejected`: ingest answered 401 at the dial, so nothing ran.

manifestRequest.description: `POST /manifest`: a registration token (the dial check) and the app's entry point from sectr.toml.

entry.description: `module:attribute` (or a bare module), as in sectr.toml's `agent.entry`.

oneOf.description: The import's manifest (what `python3 -m sectr.inspect` writes: name, entry, python, routes, env names, warnings), and whether the import ran under `uv run --no-sync` because the app ships a pyproject.toml.
Ingest answered 401 at the dial. The app was not imported.
The dial failed for another reason, after about 10 s of retries. The app was not imported.

The import failed. `exit_code` is null when it never exited on its own (couldn't start, timed out, killed by a signal); `message` then says why, and also covers an import that exited 0 without a usable manifest. `stderr_tail` is the last 4 KiB of its stderr.

error.description: A refused request: 400 `bad_request`, 409 `busy` (a turn is running on this instance), 413 `too_large`.
